title: Probabilistic discount & headcount allocation scan
summary: Monte Carlo style scan that couples tiered discount offers with headcount reallocation and quantization adoption. Produces a probabilistic distribution of runway and margin outcomes under price promotions targeted at enterprise vs mid-market. Output is a compact sheet for scenario comparison and follow-up A/B triggers.
assumptions: Base hosted API average revenue per 1k tokens = $0.55
Enterprise conversion uplift from targeted discount = 3–9 percentage points (scenario dependent)
Quantization adoption reduces per-token GPU cost by 10–30% depending on model mix
GPU spot vs reserved mix assumed: baseline 40% spot / 60% reserved
Headcount reallocation (infra -> solutions) can be executed in 6–12 weeks with partial productivity drag
SLA penalty cost per 1% outage for enterprise customers = $40k / month applied in high risk scenarios

S4,Wide sale - 25% sitewide,25,all,12,45,-6,6,18,-7.8,fast runway shortening; high SLA risk due to burst
S5,Quantization-first push - no discount but aggressive quant adoption,0,all,45,30,-3,2,30,3.5,cost reduction offsets low price movement
S7,Surge demand + discount - 20% with 60% chance of traffic spike,20,all,20,50,-8,8,12,-12.6,stress case for ops
scenario_highlights: S1: Control; use as normalization for monthly burn and headcount baseline
S2: Low risk, negative margin delta; recommended as limited-time mid-market experiment with guardrails
S3: High ROI if conversion materializes; requires SLA buffer and dedicated on-call cover during pilot
S4: Worst margin outcome; only consider with strict burst-capacity contracts and transient couponing
S5: Best long-term runway extension; prioritize infra engineering effort and onboarding plan
S6: Balanced; good tradeoff between revenue stimulus and cost savings, candidate for A/B test
S7: Stress test; triggers emergency capacity protocol and hiring freeze for 12 weeks
notes:
Observations and next steps:
- Run 10k Monte Carlo draws on S3 with enterprise account-level elasticity priors (use historical 18-mo cohort).
- Define canary signal: enterprise conversion lift >= 4pp after 8 weeks to expand S3.
- If S5 engineering effort approved, convert 30% of traffic to quantized serving in Q1 and measure real per-token cost delta.
- Map headcount reallocations into hiring plan: 1 infra -> 1 solutions for each $350k of expected new ARR to preserve delivery SLAs.
- Open questions: acceptable SLA_risk_index threshold for invoking burst-cost recapture; legal implications of targeted discounts in EU.
- Owners: Marcus for modeling, Riley for SLA/playbook, Priya for pricing comms.
